title: KV region-hinted allocator + stochastic evictor with burst spill scheduler
author: Leah Moroz
description:
Context: production workloads have exhibited sustained tail-latency amplification and higher than expected memory fragmentation in tenant KV caches when sequence length distributions vary dramatically between tenants. This PR introduces a two-part runtime change: (1) a lightweight region-hinting allocator that biases placement to minimize cross-region fragmentation and create eviction-friendly hot islands; (2) a stochastic region-prioritized evictor combined with a burst spill scheduler that coordinates async spillouts to external tiering when memory pressure spikes.

Motivation: previous evictors treated pages uniformly which worsened fragmentation for mixed-tenancy traffic. During bursty workloads the existing spill path serialized many pages and caused head-of-line stalls. The new approach reduces fragmentation score by consolidating same-lifecycle pages and schedules spill I/O in bounded bursts to avoid saturating PCIe/remote storage and blocking the fast path.

Design summary: region-hinting allocator adds a compact metadata hint on allocation (4 bytes) indicating "lifecycle class" and tenant affinity. Allocator attempts same-region placement using a fast path that prefers recently free buckets. The stochastic evictor periodically samples resident segments and scores them using a combination of residency age, fragmentation density, and hint-match score; eviction candidates are selected with weighted sampling to retain high hint-coherence. The burst spill scheduler introduces backpressure windows and token-bucket limits for async spill jobs; it groups pages by destination shard and issues coalesced write batches to reduce per-request latency.

Key behavior changes: - Reduced cross-tenant interleaving of hot/cold pages. - Evictions favor segments that free contiguous ranges to reduce fragmentation. - Spillouts are rate-limited during sustained pressure, preventing I/O from affecting generating latency. - Fallthrough behavior: when spill queue is saturated, the evictor will favor compress-on-evict (local quantized serialization) before remote spill.

Checklist: - [x] unit tests for allocator alignment and hint propagation - [x] integration test for eviction scoring under mixed workload - [x] stress benchmark showing fragmentation metric improvement - [x] CI build + linters - [x] docs: operator tuning guide

Rollout/Compatibility: feature gate KV_REGION_HINTS (off by default). Default config keeps previous eviction strategy unless enabled. Docs include recommended tuning knobs for burst_spill_tokens (default 16), spill_group_size (default 32 pages), and sampling_rate (default 0.02).

Impact: bench runs (see bench/kv/fragmentation_test.py) show a 28-44% reduction in fragmentation score on mixed short/long sequence replay and 12% lower 99p tail latency in synthetic tenant-switch workloads. Expected small uptick in memory metadata (~0.3% per-cache) due to hint bytes.

Notes: this is intended to be an iterative improvement; follow-ups will add adaptive learning of lifecycle classes from telemetry and an optional defragmenter pass during low-load windows.

review_thread: Arjun Patel: Can you explain why we prefer stochastic sampling vs deterministic LRU scanning? Deterministic scans helped explainability for SRE.
